title: Lab Automation Capex Split Across Three Requisitions in 40 Days
scenario_text:
A capital-controls audit agent at Hartwell Labs is reviewing spend on a single lab-automation project.

**Capital Expenditure Authority Matrix**
- Up to $100,000: Department Head.
- $100,001-$500,000: VP Finance AND CFO.
- Above $500,000: CFO AND CEO AND Board capital committee.
- Aggregation rule: capital purchases supporting one project or asset within a rolling 90-day window are aggregated, and the combined value sets the required approval tier. Requisitions may not be sized to keep each below a threshold.

**ERP Requisition Records (project code PRJ-LAB7, 'Automated liquid-handling line')**
- REQ-201: robotic arm module, $96,000, approved by Department Head (Dr. Lin), 2026-07-02.
- REQ-207: plate-handling module, $92,000, approved by Department Head (Dr. Lin), 2026-07-21.
- REQ-215: integration + controller cabinet, $88,000, approved by Department Head (Dr. Lin), 2026-08-11.
- All three cite PRJ-LAB7 and describe components of the same automation line.

**Email trail (reconstructed)**
- Lab manager: 'Vendor quoted the full line at ~$276K. If we buy it as one requisition it goes to VP Finance and the CFO.'
- Dr. Lin (Department Head): 'Break it into the three modules by phase so each stays under my $100K sign-off; I'll approve each as it comes.'
- Procurement: 'Understood - three requisitions raised under PRJ-LAB7.'

No VP Finance or CFO approval exists on any of the three requisitions.
question: Considering the aggregation rule, at what tier should this expenditure have been authorized? Name the required approver(s).
